## Bayesian Clinical Trials

To prove, check or extend a result of this book, start with its catalog: each of the 12 results has its exact statement, its status (proved or computed), its assumptions, its origin, its printed number and page, and the Quarto file of its source. The numbers and pages are those of version 1.3.0 of the PDF. Cite the book and the number of the result.

- [Bayesian Clinical Trials](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/index.html.md): by Alexandra Sokolova, Vadim Sokolov and Nicholas G. Polson (2026). Bayesian clinical trials built up from the traditional trial and tied to regulation: calibration, monitoring, safety, borrowing, adaptive designs, and reanalyses of landmark trials, with an R package and an online lab. Keywords: Bayesian clinical trials, adaptive trial design, group sequential design, interim monitoring, type I error calibration, FDA Bayesian guidance, multiplicity and shrinkage, informative priors, e-values, operating characteristics simulation, biostatistics, R package.
- [How to cite](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24163054): DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24163054 for version 1.3.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24122875 for all versions); the BibTeX entry is on the book page
- [Results by chapter](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html.md): 12 results with their statements, status and numbers
- [Catalog of results](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/RESULTS.md): 12 results with their statements, status and printed numbers
- [Catalog as data](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/results.yaml): the same results as YAML, each with id, label, name, chapter, origin, status, conditions, summary and statement
- [All facts as JSON](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/main/site/book.json): title, authors, DOIs, licenses, links, citation, chapters with summaries, and every result with its printed number, page, source file and LaTeX label
- [The book as a PDF](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/releases/download/v1.3.0/bayesian_clinical_trials.pdf): 610 pages, CC BY 4.0
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/tree/v1.3.0): the Quarto source, code and bibliography
- [Report an error or ask a question](https://github.com/VadimSokolov/bayesian_clinical_trials/issues): the issues of the book's repository on GitHub
- [The book as a website](https://vsokolov.org/bayesian_clinical_trials/): every chapter as a page, with search
- [Main result: The three deviation scales (evidence tolls)](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#evidence_tolls_three_scales): Section 12.9.1, page 257, proved. A fixed level test, a Bayes rule and an anytime valid rule act at three different sizes of the squared standardized score; for the normal mixture the anytime valid bar exceeds the Bayes bar by a surcharge that is about 2 log(1/alpha) at large information.
- [Main result: The surcharge for validity at every stopping time is about 70 per cent of the fixed trial requirement, as a comparison of boundary terms](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#surcharge_seventy_percent): Section 12.9.3, page 259, proved. For the normal mixture e value rule, against the uncalibrated Bayes factor bar (posterior odds of one), the large information surcharge 7.38 is about 70 per cent of the fixed trial standardized requirement 10.51; this compares boundary terms and is not an exact sample size identity.
- [Main result: Moderate deviation sample size equation](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#moderate_deviation_sample_size): Section 10.3.1, page 210, proved. A Bayes rule whose bar grows like the logarithm of the sample size has an implicit sample size equation, the textbook formula with the critical value replaced by the square root of log n plus a constant.
- [Main result: Calibration of a posterior probability rule by the null maximum](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#null_maximum_calibration): Section 15.4, page 306, proved. The smallest threshold that holds a monitored posterior probability rule to level alpha is the (1 minus alpha) quantile of the largest posterior probability reached over the looks in null simulations, so one simulation serves every threshold.
- [Main result: Exact backward induction for binary endpoints on a cubic lattice](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#backward_induction_states): Section 16.6.2, page 338, proved. For a two arm binary trial the Bayes optimal stopping rule depends only on the success counts and the stage, so backward induction is exact on a lattice of order T cubed states.
- [Main result: SELECT reconstruction, median events at decision with conditioning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#select_reconstruction_medians): Section 22.1.1, page 463, computed. In our reconstruction of SELECT at hazard ratio 0.80, a calibrated Bayesian rule stops at a median of 464 events among trials that declare efficacy and 486 over all trials, against 817 for SELECT's planned design (one interim analysis with Lan-DeMets spending, then the final); the e value rule and a four look design are slower or less powerful.
- [Main result: Reproduction of the BNT162b2 beta binomial analysis](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#bnt162b2_beta_binomial_reproduction): Section 6.6, page 118, computed. The statistical analysis plan's beta binomial model with a Beta(0.700102, 1) prior, applied to 8 versus 162 cases, gives a posterior probability that vaccine efficacy exceeds 30 per cent of 1 minus 2e-28 and a point estimate of 95 per cent, matching the published interval within a tenth of a point.
- [Computed: Reproduction of the BNT162b2 beta binomial analysis](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#bnt162b2_beta_binomial_reproduction): Section 6.6, page 118
- [Computed: The Bayes factor bar exceeds the fixed level bar once information times prior variance passes about 46](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#bayes_bar_crossing_46): Section 8.5.1, page 157
- [Computed: Moderate deviation and textbook sizes at the SELECT hazard ratio of 0.80 (not a prediction of SELECT's size)](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#moderate_deviation_select_comparison): Section 10.3.5, page 214
- [Computed: Four operation ulcer trial, adjusted p value against posterior probability](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#ulcer_bonferroni_vs_posterior): Section 11.5.2, page 236
- [Computed: A utility only backward induction rule declares treatment better half the time under the null](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#utility_only_rule_null_declaration): Section 16.6.3, page 341
- [Computed: Shared control false positive counts for four arms](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#shared_control_false_positive_counts): Section 21.4.1, page 441
- [Computed: SELECT reconstruction, median events at decision with conditioning](https://vsokolov.org/books/bayesian_clinical_trials/results.html#select_reconstruction_medians): Section 22.1.1, page 463
